fields.title: Split data access into a single-threaded caller and a thread-safe result handler, for sharded and non-sharded queries alike
fields.decision: Every ArgentSea data method follows the query paradigm, in this order. The caller declares parameters in a free-standing parameter collection before any connection exists. ArgentSea then opens a connection and command per target database, copies the parameters onto each command, executes, and passes each connection's results to a result handler. In a fan-out query this runs concurrently, one handler invocation per shard. The same structure is used for non-sharded databases. The Mapper provides the handlers for Map methods; Query methods take a caller-written handler.
fields.context: Standard ADO.NET code creates a connection, then a command, then fills that command's parameters, then reads results inline. A sharded query reverses the first steps: one parameter set must be executed on many connections at once, each on its own thread with its own command. Parameter objects cannot be shared across commands, and result-reading code runs concurrently on several connections.

alternatives.option: The conventional connection-first ADO.NET sequence, with a separate API for sharded access.
alternatives.whyRejected: Two programming models would mean two sets of habits, tests and Mapper integrations, and code would have to be rewritten when a database later becomes sharded.

alternatives.option: Sharing one parameter collection across concurrent commands.
alternatives.whyRejected: ADO.NET parameters belong to one command, and concurrent executions would overwrite each other's values and outputs.

fields.consequences: Sharded and non-sharded data access look identical, and moving a database to a shard set changes little code. Result handlers must be thread-safe, and they receive the shard id and connection description so that results and logs can be attributed. Because parameters are copied per connection, a caller cannot read output values through references held to the original parameter objects; outputs are read from the handler's collection, or through MapOutput. The parameter collection needs no command, which is why `ParameterCollection` exists.
